column1: # What each unit of tests/baseline/units.txt used, on the generated dataset
# `small` on a simulated disk with the default settings. A harness run fails
# when a unit reads, writes or syncs more than this (every column but
# memory). Written by `qdb-harness --update-baseline`; a commit that changes

column12: cat src/*.c | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 5
echo a b c | xargs -n 1 echo
grep -q kadifo src/main.c && echo found || echo none
i=0; while [ $i -lt 10000 ]; do i=$((i+1)); done; echo $i
i=10; until [ $i -eq 0 ]; do i=$((i-1)); done; echo $i
for f in src/*.c; do echo "$f"; done | wc -l
for f in src/*.c; do grep -c kadifo "$f"; done | sort -n | tail -n 3
n=0; for f in src/*.c; do if grep -q zealto "$f"; then n=$((n+1)); fi; done; echo $n
for f in src/*.c; do if [ -s "$f" ]; then continue; fi; echo "$f"; done
H=$PWD; for d in src/mod_01 docs/mod_01/mod_02 src; do cd "$d"; ls | wc -l; cd "$H"; done
find docs/mod_01/mod_02 -name '*.c' | while read -r f; do wc -l < "$f"; done | sort -n | tail -n 1
for f in src/*.c; do head -n 1 "$f"; done > /dev/null
for i in 1 2 3; do for j in a b; do if [ $i -eq 2 ]; then break; fi; echo $i$j; done; done
awk '/kadifo/ { n++ } END { print n }' src/*.c
awk '{ s += NF } END { print s, NR }' src/*.c
awk -F: '{ s += $3 } END { print s }' src/*.c
awk 'length($0) > 100 { n++ } END { print n + 0 }' src/*.c
awk '{ c[$1]++ } END { for (k in c) n++; print n }' src/*.c
awk '{ for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if ($i == "kadifo") n++ } END { print n }' src/*.c
awk -v OFS=- '{ $1 = NR; print }' src/main.c | tail -n 1
awk 'BEGIN { for (i = 0; i < 100000; i++) s += i * i; printf "%d\n", s }'
grep -rn cojokane . | awk -F: '{ print $1 }' | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 5
cat src/*.c | awk 'NF > 3 { print $1, $NF }' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 5
find docs/mod_01/mod_02 -name '*.c' | sort | xargs cat > bench_out/joined.txt
sed -i -e '10s/$/ changed/' -e '40,45d' -e '100i an added line' bench_out/v2.txt
sed -i '1s/^/one edit /' $(find bench_out/dir_copy -type f | sort | head -n 1)
for i in $(seq 10000); do echo "line $i" >> bench_out/loop.txt; done
for f in bench_out/work/*.c; do echo done >> "$f"; done
